Here's a summary of recent developments in high-tech sectors from U.S. government entities, prominent companies, and investors, along with a table of recently launched 2x leveraged single-stock ETFs.

### Quantum Technology

The U.S. government has significantly increased its focus and investment in quantum technology. In May 2026, the Department of Commerce announced letters of intent to provide $2 billion in CHIPS Act funding to nine quantum computing companies, with the government taking equity stakes. IBM is set to receive $1 billion to establish a quantum chip foundry, while GlobalFoundries is slated for $375 million. Other recipients include Quantinuum, Rigetti, D-Wave, Infleqtion, and PsiQuantum, each expecting around $100 million.

President Trump signed executive orders in June 2026 to advance quantum computing, cybersecurity, and sensors, directing the Pentagon to field three new types of quantum sensors by fall 2028 and collaborate with the Department of Energy (DoE) on building a quantum supercomputer. The DoD also released its post-quantum cryptography strategy in June 2026.

In the contracting space, the Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) issued a Special Notice in October 2025 for its Quantum Benchmarking Initiative (QBI) 2026 Solicitation, seeking novel approaches for fault-tolerant quantum computing. Infleqtion (formerly Coldquanta, Inc.) secured a $20 million contract for quantum technology maturation and design, and the Defense Innovation Unit (DIU) awarded Vector Atomic Inc. a $20.8 million agreement for "Quantum Space Sensors."

### Drone Technology

U.S. government entities are heavily investing in drone and counter-drone technologies. The Department of War (DoW) launched its $1.1 billion Drone Dominance Program in December 2025, a multi-phase initiative through 2027 to develop low-cost, one-way attack small unmanned aerial systems.

The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) established a new office in January 2026 to rapidly procure and deploy drone and counter-drone technologies, finalizing a $115 million investment for America250 and FIFA 2026 security. DHS also sought proposals for a new $1.5 billion contract vehicle for Customs and Border Protection (CBP) and Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) for advanced counter-drone systems. Additionally, the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) awarded $250 million in grants to 11 states and the National Capital Region for counter-drone capabilities related to the FIFA 2026 World Cup.

In July 2026, the Pentagon awarded AeroVironment an $80.5 million task order for AI-enabled technologies to defend Air Force bases against small drones, part of a larger $500 million Army contract. Safe Pro Group announced in August 2026 that its AI-powered drone threat-detection orders for the year surpassed $5 million, stemming from contracts with the U.S. Army, U.S. Air Force, and defense prime contractors.

NASA's ambitious Dragonfly mission, a nuclear-powered drone designed to explore Saturn's moon Titan, began its integration and testing phases in 2026, with the fuselage delivered in July 2026. Dragonfly is slated for launch in July 2028 and will be the first controlled aircraft to fly on another celestial body.

### Robotics

While no standalone major robotics announcements were explicitly highlighted in the search results, robotics often overlaps with drone and AI technologies. For instance, the AI-enabled drone defense systems mentioned above incorporate robotic elements.

### Space Technology and Satellite Communication

The U.S. Space Force has been active in developing advanced satellite communication networks. In May 2026, SpaceX was awarded a $2.29 billion contract to build the Space Data Network (SDN) Backbone, a secure, high-speed satellite communications network for military applications, with a prototype due by the end of 2027.

In August 2026, the Space Force further contracted Amazon LEO for Government, Lockheed Martin, Northrop Grumman, Rocket Lab, and York Space Systems, awarding each $12 million. These contracts aim to demonstrate interoperability for the SDN architecture, particularly focusing on optical laser communication terminals. Rocket Lab also secured delivery orders totaling $12 million to support the SDN-B program for secure optical communications in space.

Additionally, Viasat selected Rocket Lab to build a satellite bus for the U.S. Space Force's Protected Tactical SATCOM-Global (PTS-G) program. Viasat had previously been awarded a prime contract in May 2026 for one of the first small, maneuverable geosynchronous Earth orbit (GEO) satellites for the PTS-G constellation.

### Nuclear Energy

The U.S. Department of Energy (DoE) is championing a "nuclear renaissance." In July 2026, the DoE selected Utah, Tennessee, Oklahoma, Louisiana, and Idaho as potential host states for Nuclear Lifecycle Innovation Campuses. These campuses are envisioned as integrated regional nuclear ecosystems covering the full nuclear lifecycle. The DoE plans to select three of these five finalists by the end of 2026.

Significant progress has been made on advanced reactor projects. Three DoE Reactor Pilot Program reactors (Aalo, Antares, and Valar) received Documented Safety Analysis (DSA) approval and were on track for criticality by July 4, 2026. Antares achieved zero-power criticality at Idaho National Laboratory in June 2026. Furthermore, Kairos Power's HERMES II reactor in Oak Ridge, TN (which will provide energy to a Google datacenter), and Terrapower's Natrium reactor in Kemmerer, Wyoming, began nuclear side construction in May 2026.

Other DoE initiatives in 2026 include the Utility Power Reactor Incremental Scaling Effort (UPRISE), launched in March 2026, aiming to add 2.5 GW of nuclear capacity by 2027 and 5 GW by 2029. The DoE also established the Nuclear Energy Launch Pad in March 2026 to promote advanced nuclear technologies and announced a $2.7 billion investment in January 2026 to strengthen domestic uranium enrichment. In April 2026, Senators Lee and McCormick introduced the Nuclear Energy Innovation and Deployment Act (NEIDA) to accelerate the deployment of next-generation nuclear energy technologies.

### Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Latest Innovative Technologies

The U.S. government is aggressively pushing an "AI-first" agenda, particularly within defense. The Department of War (DoW) issued multiple memoranda and a speech in January 2026, outlining a wartime-speed strategy to achieve "America's Military AI Dominance," with seven "Pace-Setting Projects" for fiscal year 2026. The DoD's AI spending significantly outpaced other federal agencies in 2026, accounting for 98.9% of all potential federal AI contract value, totaling $90.7 billion across 1,319 contracts.

In June 2026, a new AI Incident Reporting Program was proposed for the draft FY2027 National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) for the DoD, which would include mechanisms for protected disclosures from military personnel, civilian employees, and contractors. The DoW introduced GenAI.mil in December 2025, a bespoke generative AI platform featuring Google Cloud's Gemini for Government.

In the private sector, Microsoft and the General Services Administration (GSA) signed a deal worth up to $3.1 billion in January 2026 to provide discounted AI services to federal agencies, including free Copilot access for up to 12 months. An Executive Order on AI Innovation and Security, signed on June 2, 2026, aims to accelerate AI adoption by establishing a cybersecurity clearinghouse for AI-powered systems and creating a voluntary framework for agencies to access frontier models early.
